Title: News from the Liaison: Jyhad Card Backs

Messages.Author: Thomas R Wylie
Messages.Body:
In my post of a few days ago about Jyhad's upcoming name change, I said 
that the card backs would be changed to read Vampire: The Eternal 
Struggle instead of Jyhad.  As it turns out, this is incorrect.

The V:TES team has decided that only the Vampire card backs will change.  
The green library cards will continue to say "Jyhad," and will therefore 
be indistiguishable from cards being sold now.

This is a compromise between people who felt that the card backs should 
be changed, and people who felt that the change would be too disruptive.  
Since it is a compromise, I expect that no one will be completely happy 
with it, but I hope that most players will find it a reasonable solution.

Thanks for your continued patience.

Kathy Ice
Cyberspace Liaison
Wizards of the Coast, Inc.
liaison@wizards.com
kice@wizards.com

Let me ask the question: How much do any of you out there believe that
a compromise between player/collectors (who said, "hey, don't change
the card backs") and WotC (who said first, "The game isn't selling well
so we are changing the name," and then said, "The name Jyhad is so
offensive that we must change the name") is to only rename the
vampire card backs?

Here's how I see it. Players will still have to replace some (not all,
which i guess is a compromise) of their cards. WotC on the other
hand gains nothing. I'm not sure how cards inside a package
are going to change buying habits. I also see how the word is any
less offesive if it only appears on vampire cards. Give me a break.

Since WotC gets nothing by changing the backs and the players get
the benifit of only having to re-purchase a portion of their decks,
a better compromise is not to change the backs at all & only
chage the boxes and booster decks. WotC gains whatever marketing
edge they think a name change will bring. They don't get the moral
high ground by still using the word Jyhad, but they don't get that
in the current compromise anyway. The players get to keep all
their cards that they have already purchased without having 
to reinvest more to get what they already own. Hmmm...may not sound
like much of a compromise, but changing only the vampire card backs
doesn't even count as eye wash on this farce that has become Jyhad.

Sign me as one disillusioned former customre of WotC. (Yes, I
actually do give my money to companies I like and withhold it from
ones that shaft me)

Ned

Messages.Author: Andrew B. Kaiser
Messages.Body:
Ned Flanders (tripwire@access.digex.net) wrote:
: aahz@cats.ucsc.edu (Thomas R Wylie) writes:



: Sign me as one disillusioned former customre of WotC. (Yes, I
: actually do give my money to companies I like and withhold it from
: ones that shaft me)

: Ned

I for one am very content with the change made. I'm looking at the situation
from a different angle: What if they decided to rename the library cards, too?
Then the games would be really screwed. Whereas the crypt cards aren't that
big of a deal. Think about it: Seeing as how I can buy the new boosters knowing
that the library cards will be identical to the old, I'm probably going to buy
quite a bit. And I'm sure these new boosters will have the usual vampires in
them. And these vampires will most likely be new ones. But, my point is- how
much can they change the actual vampires so that the player using them has
an advantage over someone who isn't? Yes, there might be new special abilities,
and the clans might have different disipline combinations, but as far as the
vampires go, there will be no drastic changes. I'd be happy to use these marked
crypt cards in exchange for usable library cards. 
Yes, this is a compromise, but I think it's one I can live with.

Andy

Messages.Author: Jon Inge Teigland
Messages.Body:
Ned Flanders (tripwire@access.digex.net) wrote:
: 
: Here's how I see it. Players will still have to replace some (not all,
: which i guess is a compromise) of their cards. WotC on the other
: hand gains nothing. I'm not sure how cards inside a package
: are going to change buying habits. I also see how the word is any
: less offesive if it only appears on vampire cards. Give me a break.
: 
Ok, I admit it, I haven't been following this thread too closely, but 
anyway I wonder: Why do you have to replace your cards ? Have WotC said
that the 'old' cards are illegal in tournament play ? I can't understand 
that they should be. WotC still accept Magic Alpha cards in tournament 
play even though they are distinguishable from the rest of the cards. 
You may say that playing with only SOME 'old' cards, or specifically
playing with only ONE 'old' card will be the same as playing with marked 
cards. I will agree with that, but the same counts for Magic Alpha cards.
I can understand that WotC can rule that you have to use EITHER 'old'
cards, OR 'new' cards, but not mix them. This is the strictest ruling I 
can understand should ever be nessecary. I would rather have a ruling that
if you use a mix of 'old' and 'new' cards, there should be at least 
something like 40% of each, or in other words, an even distribution.
If you ask me (which you don't, but anyway) I assume the 'old' cards will 
be worth more to a collector, simply because of this namechange. Hang on
to your cards for a year or two, and THEN see if you are sorry for the 
change. If they had changed the back of the library cards too, I would 
have considered it identically to the change between Magic Alpha and Beta
cards. And since they so far have not banned Magic Alpha cards from 
tournament play, I can see no reason why they should have banned the 
Jyhad Alpha cards either.

If you desparately want to, you can try to make me change my mind, but I
don't recomend it.

Jon Inge Teigland, who loves Jyhad, and don't give a damn about the 
namechange.

Messages.Author: Bob Ellison
Messages.Body:
> Ok, I admit it, I haven't been following this thread too closely, but 
> anyway I wonder: Why do you have to replace your cards ? Have WotC said
> that the 'old' cards are illegal in tournament play ? I can't understand 
> that they should be. WotC still accept Magic Alpha cards in tournament 
> play even though they are distinguishable from the rest of the cards. 

The problem is the risk of "marked" or "semimarked" cards.  Essentially,
you're now allowed to mark the backs of all your vampire cards with one
of two symbols (i.e. two distinguishing backs).  I can think of many 
ways I can use those marks.  Perhaps in my Toreador/Brujah deck, all
my Toreador are marked with one, and all my Brujah with another; then
I know what's coming.

Perhaps more abusively, what if I mark all my low-weight vampires (those
with capacity 4 or less) with one back, and all my higher-weight 
vampires with another?  Not only can I tell what's coming in my crypt,
but when I shuffle my cards, I can make sure that I end up with
a low-weight vampire on top, so I know I can bring out at least one
minion quickly (let me tell you about the time the top four vampires
of my crypt were all my biggest vampires: 3 10-pointers and an 8-pointer... 
my predator didn't even *need* stealth to bleed the crap out of me in 
the first few rounds).  With markings like this, you can also tell
whether, late in the game, it might be worth the effort to pull out
a new vampire...

Some people don't think this is much of an advantage.  But every little
bit counts.  If my opponents don't mind me playing with marked cards,
great! :-)  If they do, and I have to stick with one set of backs or
the other, either I won't be able to use my vast collection of old
vampire cards, or I won't be able to use expansion vampires.  I'm not
thrilled with either option.

> If you desparately want to, you can try to make me change my mind, but I
> don't recomend it.

:-)  No, that's not my goal.  I just want you to understand *mine*.  
I think you've expressed your opinion very well, very completely; I
think I have a good "handle" on it.  I hope I've done the same.

papillo the master debater

Quite simply, we make sure that all their crypt cards are facing the same
driection. The crypt is small enough to easily shuffle and keep the cards
oriented properly. We've also gotten in the habit of shuffling our libraries
in such a way that they're all the same direction. Simple solution. (Unlike
the problem with different crypt cardbacks)

Messages.Author: Ned Flanders
Messages.Body:
tidleman@sj.unisys.com (The Bomb) writes:

>Ned,

>Let me ask this:  How many vampires are you going to need to replace?  

>It is fairly easy to get one of every vampire in the current Jyhad printing.  
>And the vampires would be the only cards you would need to replace if the 
>crypt cards still say "Jyhad".  So I think you're blowing things out of 
>proportion.  

>Now if WoTC said they would change the backs of the crypt cards while keeping 
>the backs of the vampire cards the same, I think you'd have a valid point.

>Thanks,
>The Bomb

Since I collect as well as play, I will need to get a full set
of new vamps plus a playing set...if they have just the
same old vamps thats 121 (I think that's all but I don't recall)
plus the 30-ish that rotate thru the crypt. at four per pack
(assuming the ratios stay the same and we ignore the non-vamp
vamp cards) that is approx. 37 packs (assuming I can trade all dups
to get a complete set, a reasonable assumption) at $2.75 per pack
comes to just over $100

Admittedly, I will also be getting a bunch of presumably new library
cards in the process so the full $100 is not just for vamps. Let's just
call it 4/19 of the total for $21 for new vamps. My question is why
should i pay $21 for something I already own that WotC has chosen to 
make obsolete? It's not the end of the world, and you may consider
it to be blown out of proportion, but I don't like to be shafted by 
companies in what appears to be no more than a shameless attempt
to get more money FROM PEOPLE WHO HAVE ALREADY BOUGHT INTO THE GAME.

There have been numerous post going into why chaning card backs inside
packs do nothing to boost new sales (inside the pack = no visibility,
new name = visibility) while a new name seems like a good idea or at
least not objectionable.

Hope that clears up why I think it is something worth sounding off
about.

Ned

>shuffle another's deck.

If this is the way you play, then you can still screw up someone who is trying
to mark things using card orientation.  Cut the deck, rotating the cut 180
degrees.  Then ask the player to shuffle again.  That destroys and such marking
scheme, and you don't have to worry about harming each other's cards.

	Alec

Messages.Author: Danny Oscar Kip
Messages.Body:
Keith A. Arner (kraven@keystone.westminster.edu) wrote:

: Well, to throw the idea onto the table, is it feasible that WotC would be
: comsumer friendly (such as they were with the Legends mix-up) and offer
: to replace Vampires with the Jyhad card back for Vampires with the
: V:tES card back on a one-for-one basis?

Dream on, they'd lose money then.

: If WotC made such an offer, I don't see how anyone could accuse them of
: being anything but fair in this matter, even if the consumer had to pay
: a very nominal fee (nothing much more than SASE or similar).

Just remember you said 'if'.

Oh another thing, WotC says Jyhad isn't very popular now, so they
don't care about those 'few' that have bought it so far.
They expect to get so many new customers they don't need them.
Over here, in Groningen, The Netherlands, we intend to boycot any
cards that don't have a 'Jyhad' back, or for that matter a different
edge then the current black one. (we'd hate white or yellow the most)

I hope they change their mind and just change the packaging and the
name of the game.
--
